title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE LAPSE OF CRIMINAL SENTENCES
title_original: 형의 실효 등에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters mandated by the Act on the Lapse of Criminal Sentences and those necessary for the enforcement thereof. <Amended on Jul. 27, 2006; Jul. 5, 2022>

Article 2 (Preparation of Investigation Material Cards) (1) Investigation materials cards shall include the following: <Amended on Jul. 5, 2022>
  1. Personal information, such as the name, nationality, resident registration number, alien registration number (limited to where the criminal suspect is a foreigner), passport number (limited to where the suspect has no resident registration number or alien registration number), etc. of the criminal suspect;
  2. Investigative or criminal records, such as the name of a crime, booking agency and date, disposition results and sentencing results.
  (2) Heads of investigation agencies, such as public prosecutors' offices and judicial police authorities, shall, without delay, send the National Police Agency the records of criminal suspects booked and the details of dispositions or sentences against such suspects, etc. in order to correctly manage the investigation materials cards. <Amended on Apr. 2, 2024>
  (3) Where it is impossible to confirm the details of dispositions and sentences due to any inconsistency in the personal information of criminal suspects on the investigation materials cards and other reasons, the Commissioner General of the National Police Agency shall take necessary measures to keep accurate records of dispositions and sentences by seeking confirmation from the agencies concerned or other means. <Newly Inserted on Apr. 2, 2024>
  (4) In making investigation materials cards, the scope of criminal suspects to be fingerprinted and other necessary matters shall be determined by Ordinance of the Ministry of Justice. <Amended on Apr. 2, 2024>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 1985]
  [Title Amended on Sep. 29, 2003]

Article 2-2 Deleted. <Jul. 5, 2022>

Article 3 (Recording on Convict Lists by High Prosecutors’ Offices) Where a judgment imposing the suspension of qualifications or a heavier punishment becomes final and conclusive in proceedings to appeal a military court decision, the relevant high prosecutors' office may also record such facts on a convict list. <Amended on Oct. 6, 1984; Sep. 4, 1993; Jun. 30, 2022>
  [Title Amended on Jun. 30, 2022]

Article 4 (Preparing and Sending of Convict Plates) Where the fact that a judgment imposing the suspension of qualifications or a heavier punishment becomes final and conclusive is entered on a convict list in accordance with Article 3 of the Act on the Lapse of Criminal Sentences (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") and Article 3 of this Decree, a convict plate shall, without delay, be prepared and sent to a Si/Gu/Eup/Myeon office of the place of registration of the convict by registered mail or by electronic means through the Public Information Sharing Center under Article 37 (1) of the Electronic Government Act. <Amended on Oct. 6, 1984; Aug. 7, 2007; May 4, 2010; Apr. 23, 2012; Jul. 5, 2022>

Article 5 (Notification of Lapse of Suspension of Execution) Where any case falling under any of the subparagraphs of Article 4 (2) of the Act occurs, the district prosecutors’ office, their branch office, or the military prosecutor’s office, which have sent convict plates according to Article 4 shall, without delay, notify the government offices to which they have sent the convict plates of the fact by registered mail or by electronic means through the Public Information Sharing Center established under Article 37 (1) of the Electronic Government Act: Provided, That where they have additionally stated in advance the period of suspension of execution or the period of lapse of punishment under Article 7 of the Act in the convict plates which are sent pursuant to Article 4, such additional statement may substitute for the fact that the period of suspension of execution has lapsed in the notification of reasons under the subparagraphs of Article 4 (2) of the Act, or notification of the fact that the punishment imposed under Article 7 of the Act has lapsed. <Amended on May 4, 2010; Jun. 30, 2022>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Aug. 7, 2007]

Article 6 (Scope of Judicial Police Officers in Charge of Preparing Investigation Materials Cards) The scope of judicial police officers to prepare investigation materials cards pursuant to the main clause, with the exception of its subparagraphs, of Article 5 (1) of the Act shall be as follows:
  1. A senior judicial police officer under Article 197 (1) of the Criminal Procedure Act;
  2. A military judicial police officer under Article 43 of the Military Court Act;
  3. A person who performs the duties of a judicial police officer under other statutes.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 5, 2022]

Article 6-2 (Preservation and Management of Criminal Records or Investigation Record Materials, and Reply to Queries) (1) The head of an agency in charge of preserving and managing criminal records or investigation record materials or the duties related with inquiries thereabout shall designate a highest official of the department in direct charge of such duties as a responsible person therefor and shall have him/ her take charge of the operation and guidance work regarding the preservation and administration of such records and materials or inquiries thereabout.
  (2) The responsible person under paragraph (1) shall keep a ledger of inquiries and replies and record the purposes of reference, the positions and names of the inquirer, the preparing person, the date of preparation, and other necessary matters in the ledger.
  (3) The head of an agency in charge of the duties of preserving and managing criminal records or investigation record materials or the duties related with inquiries thereabout shall check a ledger of inquiries and replies frequently and take other necessary measures to prevent the illegal leakage of the criminal records or the investigation record materials and the diversion of such records and materials to other purposes than the criminal investigation, trial, etc. as prescribed by the Act and other statutes.
  (4) Deleted. <Dec. 27, 2006>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 29, 2003]

Article 7 (Inquiry about Investigation Materials Cards and Extent of Reply thereto) (1) In cases falling under Article 6 (1) 1 through 4 of the Act, criminal and investigative record inquiries about the criminal record materials and the investigation record materials, and the reply thereto may be made with respect to the whole of such materials. <Amended on Jul. 5, 2022>
  (2) The scope within which inquiries about criminal records or investigation records on the investigation material cards and a reply thereto under Article 6 (1) 5 through 9 of the Act may be made shall be as follows: <Amended on Jul. 27, 2006; Nov. 4, 2015>
  1. In cases falling under Article 6 (1) 5, 6, and 8 of the Act, the criminal record materials and the investigation record materials of the cases which are in the process of criminal investigation or trial;
  2. In cases falling under Article 6 (1) 7 of the Act, the criminal record materials, and the investigation record materials of the cases wherein transference to juvenile department, suspension of prosecution, or absence of authority to institute prosecution has been determined, or which are in the process of criminal investigation or trial;
  3. In cases falling under Article 6 (1) 9 of the Act, the materials necessary to confirm the grounds for disqualifications, the specific grounds for disciplinary punishment of a public official against whom a disciplinary procedure has started or the grounds for restrictions on payment, etc. (hereinafter referred to as the "grounds for disqualifications, etc."), but if it is impracticable to specify criminal records falling under the grounds for disqualifications, etc., the materials falling under any of the following items: Provided, That for the purpose of confirming specific grounds for disciplinary punishment of a public official against whom a disciplinary procedure has started, only the following criminal record materials shall be provided:
    (a) The criminal record materials wherein the type of punishment are the same with the criminal records which may fall under the grounds for disqualifications, etc.;
    (b) The investigation record materials of the cases which are in the process of criminal investigation or trial for any criminal fact which may fall under the grounds for disqualifications, etc.
  (3) In cases falling under Article 6 (1) 10 of the Act, inquiries and replies thereto may be made only within the scope specifically determined by other Acts. <Amended on Jul. 27, 2006>
  (4) Deleted. <Dec. 28, 2007>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 29, 2003]
  [Title Amended on Dec. 28, 2007]

Article 7-2 (Restriction on Reply Regarding Juveniles and Lapsed Punishment) (1) Unless it falls under Article 7 (1), replies to inquiries regarding the transference to the Juvenile Department and protective order under the Juvenile Act shall not be made after three years pass from the time such decision was made.
  (2) Notwithstanding Article 7 (1), where the person in question him or herself requests for inquiries to confirm the details of investigation materials cards as prescribed in Article 6 (1) 4 of the Act, replies to queries shall be made except for the matters in the following subparagraphs unless the person in question requests otherwise: <Amended on Nov. 4, 2015; Apr. 2, 2024>
  1. Punishment lapsed under Article 7 of the Act or Article 81 of the Criminal Act;
  2. Punishment of a person who has been pardoned or has had his or her rights reinstated;
  3. Transfer of a juvenile to the Juvenile Department and protective detention of a juvenile as prescribed in the Juvenile Act, for whom three years have passed since such decision was made;
  4. The suspension of imposition of sentence deemed to be acquitted under Article 60 of the Criminal Act;
  5. The suspension of execution of sentence which loses its validity under Article 65 of the Criminal Act.
  (3) Notwithstanding Article 7 (1), where the person in question him or herself requests for inquiries as it is required to enter and stay in a foreign country as prescribed in Article 6 (1) 4 of the Act, replies to queries shall be made except for the following matters: <Newly Inserted on Nov. 4, 2015; Apr. 2, 2024>
  1. Punishment lapsed under Article 7 of the Act or Article 81 of the Criminal Act;
  2. Punishment invalidated after an offender has been pardoned or has had his or her rights reinstated under the Amnesty Act;
  3. Transfer of a juvenile to the Juvenile Department and protective detention of a juvenile as prescribed in the Juvenile Act, for whom three years have passed since such decision was made;
  4. The suspension of imposition of sentence deemed to be acquitted under Article 60 of the Criminal Act;
  5. The suspension of execution of sentence which loses its validity under Article 65 of the Criminal Act.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Dec. 28, 2007]

Article 8 (Adjustment of Convict Lists) (1) The deletion of any relevant column on the convict lists under Article 8 (2) of the Act shall be done by drawing two horizontal lines on the relevant columns on the convict lists, and affixing the official seal of the manager of the convict lists. <Amended on Sep. 29, 2003; Jul. 27, 2006>
  (2) The deletion of any corresponding matter in the investigation record materials under Article 8-2 (1) of the Act shall be conducted by immediately deleting the corresponding matters from electronic data when the preservation period of such investigation record materials under paragraphs (2) through (4) of that Article has passed, and the position and name of the person who has deleted, the date and time of the deletion, and other matters related to the deletion shall be electronically managed for five years from the date of the deletion. <Amended on Apr. 2, 2024>
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Sep. 4, 1993]
  [Title Amended on Sep. 29, 2003]

Article 9 (Destruction of Investigation Materials Cards) (1) When a person listed on the investigation materials cards dies, the Commissioner General of the National Police Agency may destroy the investigation materials cards concerned.
  (2) When the investigation materials cards are kept and managed and preserved in the form of microfilms or electronic data, the Commissioner General of the National Police Agency may destroy the previous investigation material cards.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Sep. 29, 2003]

Article 10 (Management of Sensitive Information and Personally Identifiable Information) The head of an agency in charge of preserving and managing investigation materials cards, criminal records or investigation record materials or the duties related with inquiries and replies thereto may manage data that constitute a criminal history record or personal information resulting from specific technical processing of data relating to the physical, physiological or behavioral characteristics of an individual under Article 18 of the Enforcement Decree of Personal Information Protection Act for the purpose of uniquely identifying that individual (limited to where the affairs referred to in subparagraph 2 are performed), and resident registration numbers, passport numbers, or alien registration numbers under subparagraph 1, 2, or 4 of Article 19 of that Enforcement Decree, if unavoidable to perform the following affairs:
  1. Affairs regarding sentenced inmate list and sentenced inmate plate under Articles 3, 4 and 8 of the Act;
  2. Affairs regarding investigation materials cards under Articles 5 and 5-2 of the Act;
  3. Affairs regarding inquiries about criminal records and investigation records and replies thereto under Article 6 of the Act;
  4. Affairs regarding the arrangement of investigation record materials under Article 8-2 of the Act;
  5. Affairs regarding the submission and correction of criminal records or investigation record materials under Article 8-3 of the Act.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Apr. 2, 2024]
